Chapter 5: Balancing Individual Dreams and Family Expectations
You know, as we grow up, there’s this moment when our own ambitions start to bump up against what our family hopes for us. It’s something almost everyone faces—especially when you start making choices that really shape your future.
In the father’s letters to Su Yen, he opens up about this kind of balancing act. He shares memories from his own youth, when the path his parents imagined for him felt both comforting and, honestly, a little stifling. There was a clear checklist—study hard, get a steady job, start a family. All of it came from love and a wish for security, but sometimes, it felt like there wasn’t much space left for taking chances or following a dream that looked a little different.
He brings up the story of a relative who decided to follow a passion for the arts, even though the family wanted something more traditional. At first, there was disappointment—maybe even some anger. But as time went on, and that relative found happiness and success, the family realized something important. True love isn’t about trying to control someone’s path. It’s about supporting them, and having the trust to let them find their own way.
And let’s be real—the pressure to live up to family expectations can feel overwhelming, especially in cultures where the group’s well-being is valued above all else. There’s always that fear—what if you let someone down, or seem ungrateful, or even rebellious? But the father reminds Su Yen that her life belongs to her. It’s okay to reach for what brings her joy, even if it means stepping off the well-trodden path.
That said, he’s not telling her to forget about family values, either. There’s so much wisdom woven into traditions—the importance of hard work, the strength of community, and learning to bounce back when things get tough. These aren’t just rules. They’re lessons, carried down through generations.
The father encourages Su Yen to have those honest, sometimes tough conversations with her family about what she hopes for, and what scares her. He shares a memory of a family meeting where everyone got to talk about their dreams, even the ones that sounded a bit wild. It wasn’t easy—there were tears, maybe some arguments—but in the end, the family felt more connected and respected each other’s wishes a little more.
And here’s something practical—compromise. Sometimes, your dreams and your family’s hopes won’t line up perfectly. In those moments, it’s about finding common ground—ways to keep moving toward what excites you while still honoring where you came from.
So, what’s the real message here? The father hopes Su Yen finds the courage to walk her own path, but also the wisdom to appreciate the steady support of family. He truly believes you can be true to yourself, without turning your back on the people who care most.
Through these stories and reflections, he paints a picture of family—not as a limit, but as a source of strength and flexibility. His hope for Su Yen, and for anyone listening, is simple: have the confidence to chase your dreams, knowing you’re rooted in a legacy of love and resilience.
